Hi Olivia — appreciate the clarity. Draft MAP attached (MAP-CloudClinic-v1.xlsx). Below is a concise plan we think will get you to a staged performance run by Jun 27 if we have the requested inputs within 48 hours.

Summary of action items (owner — eta):
1) Org invite + role mapping — CloudClinic: provide list of Redwood user emails and desired roles (owner: Olivia) — due: 2028-06-17 17:00 PDT
2) API key provisioning (scoped eval key, 7-day TTL) — Redwood: Mina (will create and share secure link) — target: 2028-06-18 11:00 PDT
3) IP allowlist (CIDR list for staging/CI) — CloudClinic/infra: provide csv (we can accept one-off entries) — due: 2028-06-17 17:00 PDT
4) VPC peering setup (request + accept handshake) — joint: CloudClinic infra to send AWS account ID & VPC CIDR, Redwood to raise peering request — request raised: 2028-06-18, accept window: 48 hours
5) Test credentials & smoke validation (short script + sample prompts) — Redwood: Grace — target: 2028-06-19
6) Performance run kickoff (2-week run) — CloudClinic + Redwood — target start: 2028-06-27

Network details we need from infra to start the peering workflow: AWS account ID, VPC ID, VPC CIDR (e.g., 10.20.0.0/16), and preferred routing policy (we default to only peering for private API egress). If you prefer to terminate in a Transit Gateway, note that in your reply.

Short-lived keys: We'll create an API key with read/write for the evaluation namespace and a token TTL of 7 days. Jonas will provide a script to rotate/renew keys if you want automated rotation during the run.

Security notes:
- All API key delivery will be via the Redwood Console secure link (one-time view).
- We will enable request-level logging for the evaluation and produce a short daily usage report.
- If SOC2 evidence or audit logs are required during the eval, tell us which artifacts you want and we can export them.

Attachments: MAP-CloudClinic-v1.xlsx (draft mutual action plan), redwood-pocexecution.png (diagram of proposed network flow)

Best,

Quick follow-up — adding a couple of implementation details before we lock the MAP: 

- API keys: we'll use scoped namespaces and rate-limits at the token layer. For CI runners we recommend a separate token with a tighter rate-limit (example: 60 req/min) so you can avoid throttling user-simulated traffic.
- IP allowlist format: prefer CSV with columns (label, cidr, owner_email). Example row: "ci-runner-01, 34.216.128.0/24, infra@cloudclinic.com"
- VPC peering: we'll open the request from our side after we receive: Account ID, VPC ID, VPC CIDR, and preferred AZs. Note: cross-account peering requires both sides to accept; we can automate retries for 72 hours if acceptance is delayed.

I'll also include a short terraform snippet in the MAP file (see worksheet 'network-snippets') so infra can paste into their environment for faster acceptance.

If CloudClinic wants us to provision a jumpbox for test egress we can do that as an optional step (estimate +8 hours).

-- Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood
